STATE AID – DENMARK & SWEDEN
State aid SA.56621(2020/FC) & SA.56622 (2020/FC) - Alleged aid to PostNord Strålfors A/S
Invitation to submit comments pursuant to Article 108(2) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union
(Text with EEA relevance)
(C/2026/5257)
By means of the letter dated 24 July 2026 reproduced in the authentic language on the pages following this summary, the Commission notified Denmark and Sweden of its decision to initiate the procedure laid down in Article 108(2) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union concerning the abovementioned aid. The Commission decided not to raise any objections to certain other measures, as described in the letter following this summary. Interested parties may submit their comments on the measures in respect of which the Commission is initiating the procedure within one month of the date of publication of this summary and the following letter, to:
European Commission,
Directorate-General Competition
State Aid Greffe
1049 Bruxelles/Brussel
BELGIQUE/BELGIË
Stateaidgreffe@ec.europa.eu
These comments will be communicated to Denmark and Sweden. Confidential treatment of the identity of the interested party submitting the comments and/or of parts of the comments submitted may be requested in writing, stating the reasons for the request. Text of summary
On 5 March 2020, the Commission received a complaint from Dansk Scanning A/S (“Dansk Scanning” or “the complainant”) regarding alleged State aid in favour of PostNord Strålfors A/S (“PNS”), a subsidiary of the PostNord Strålfors Group AB (“PNS Group”), which is in turn a subsidiary of the PostNord Group AB (“PN Group”), owned by PostNord AB (“PN AB”). PN AB is owned by Sweden (60 %) and Denmark (40 %)).

Is Article 16(5) of the SAFE Regulation ( 1 ) – in so far as it provides for a derogation from the exclusion rule laid down in Article 16(3) in favour of an economic operator which has been subject to screening within the meaning of Regulation (EU) 2019/452 ( 2 ) and has obtained investment authorisation from the government of another Member State – to be interpreted as meaning that it is such that it is binding on the contracting authority which launched and conducts a SAFE procurement procedure, and cannot be contested by that authority, which should therefore merely take note of the authorisation granted by that other Member State when deciding whether to allow the economic operator concerned to participate in the procedure;

THE COUNCIL OF THE EUROPEAN UNION,

Having regard to Council Regulation (EU) 2017/1509 concerning restrictive measures against the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea and repealing Regulation (EC) No 329/2007 ( 1 ) , and in particular Article 47(2) thereof,
Having regard to the proposal from the High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy,
Whereas:
(1)

On 11 September 2017, in United Nations Security Council Resolution (UNSCR) 2375 (2017), the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) decided to prohibit the opening, maintenance and operation of all joint ventures or cooperative entities with Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) entities or individuals. (3)
On 22 December 2017, in UNSCR 2397 (2017), the UNSC acknowledged that the proceeds of the DPRK’s trade in sectoral goods, as well as the revenue generated from DPRK workers overseas, among others, contribute to the DPRK’s nuclear weapons and ballistic missile programmes. The UNSC decided to require the repatriation of all DPRK workers abroad, subject to applicable national and international law. Furthermore, the UNSC decided to increase the existing restrictive measures in a number of sectors, including with regard to the supply, sale or transfer to the DPRK of crude oil and all refined petroleum products. (4)
On 19 December 2023, the High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy (the ‘High Representative’) issued a declaration on behalf of the Union underlining that the DPRK must comply with its obligations under UNSCRs by abandoning all its nuclear weapons, other weapons of mass destruction, ballistic missile programmes and existing nuclear programmes, in a complete, verifiable and irreversible manner and cease all related activities.
